description: A deputy general counsel must decide whether to approve a university research collaboration agreement for a clinical analytics project and set the agreement's publication, data-handling, and commercialization terms, with input from research counsel, privacy counsel, and business development counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company and Northbridge University have negotiated a draft collaboration agreement for a clinical analytics project.
shared_context.S2: The draft permits the university to receive project data, gives the university a 60-day publication review period, and grants the company nonexclusive commercialization rights across all fields.
shared_context.S3: The project is scheduled to begin next month, and the agreement is awaiting legal approval.
shared_context.S4: The firm's standard transaction review requires research, privacy, and business development counsel to give a status report before the Deputy General Counsel approves the agreement.

PF1.text: Marcus reviewed the executed terms of the NIH-funded award supporting Northbridge's work yesterday and confirmed that the collaboration agreement must give Northbridge exactly 90 days for prepublication review; the award terms are not yet uploaded to the transaction file.

PF2.text: Nina completed a data inventory this week and confirmed that the proposed dataset contains 1,240 identifiable patient records; those records may not be transferred to Northbridge, and all processing must occur in the company's controlled environment. She has not yet entered the finding in the contract checklist.

PF3.text: During a call with the business sponsor yesterday, Owen confirmed that the sponsor will approve the collaboration only if the company receives exclusive commercialization rights in the clinical-diagnostics field while retaining rights in every other field; Owen has not circulated the sponsor's condition.

acceptance_conditions: The publication review period must be exactly 90 days.
The agreement must prohibit transfer of patient-level data.
All project data processing must occur in the company's controlled environment.
The company must receive exclusive commercialization rights in clinical diagnostics while retaining rights in every other field.
The settlement must include commitments documenting the publication, data-handling, and commercialization terms.

decisive_facts.why: The draft's 60-day review changes to exactly 90 days, and a publication-review commitment becomes necessary once the NIH award term is known.
The draft's data-transfer permission changes to a prohibition and company-controlled processing once the 1,240 identifiable patient records are confirmed.
The draft's broad nonexclusive rights change to exclusive clinical-diagnostics rights with all other fields retained by the company, requiring a matching commercialization commitment.
